documents.text:
---
doc_id: doc-999fea2863cc
description: "C# formatting, imports, comments, Harmony patch and component conventions for Natural Backwalls Everywhere (adds backwalls to natural biomes during worldgen), with this mod's own layout."
applies_to:
  - "src/**"
---
# Code Style Guide

## Formatting
**Id:** blk-96ef0366d483

### Indentation
**Id:** blk-3caa04f3cdc5

- Tabs, one per level, in every `.cs` file (`mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Mod.cs`).
- Project files (`.csproj`, `common/oni-mod.props`, `common/oni-mod.targets`) use two spaces.
- Files are committed with LF line endings; Windows checkouts convert them to CRLF (`core.autocrlf` is true), so do not hand-normalise line endings.

### Line Length
**Id:** blk-81477512dcc1

- No limit is configured and the repository has no `.editorconfig`.
- Wrap long calls and string concatenations after an argument or before a `+`, and indent the continuation one tab. The start-up log call in `mods/jumper-bridges/src/JumperBridges/Mod.cs` is the pattern.
- TODO(owner): decide whether to add an `.editorconfig` recording tabs and brace placement so editors enforce what the code already does.

### Braces
**Id:** blk-24b49007faf3

- Opening brace on its own line (Allman) for namespaces, types, members and multi-line control blocks.
- A body of one short statement goes on the next line without braces:

```csharp
foreach (Mod mod in mods)
{
	if (!mod.IsEnabledForActiveDlc())
		continue;
	...
}
```

- Multi-line initialisers and enums end with a trailing comma (`YieldToWorkshopIds` in `mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Mod.cs`, `CoolPodMode` in `mods/storage-pod-redux/src/StoragePodRedux/Options.cs`).

## Language and Toolchain
**Id:** blk-4419da43d2cc

- C# 9 on .NET Framework 4.8 (`LangVersion` 9.0 and `TargetFramework` net48 in `common/oni-mod.props`). Namespace blocks, not file-scoped namespaces; no nullable reference types.
- Mods compile against the game's own assemblies (`common/oni-mod.targets`): `Assembly-CSharp`, `Assembly-CSharp-firstpass`, `0Harmony` and Unity modules. The game's .NET Framework lacks some newer APIs (`ConditionalWeakTable.AddOrUpdate` is missing, see `mods/detect-any-element/src/DetectAnyElement/Patches.cs`).
- Optional references are switched on in the mod csproj before the targets import: `ReferenceUnityUI`, `ReferenceImageConversion`, `UsePLib` (PLib is ILRepack-merged into the mod DLL) and `UseTranslations` (compiles `common/src/Translations.cs` in).
- One namespace per mod, equal to its `RootNamespace`. Subfolders organise files and do not add namespaces (`mods/upgrade-planner/src/UpgradePlanner/Plan`, `Rules`, `Tool`, `UI` all declare `namespace UpgradePlanner`).

## Imports/Includes
**Id:** blk-4e88f5e090ac

### Organization
**Id:** blk-97419ca6d969

`using` directives sit above the namespace, in one block with no blank lines, sorted alphabetically with `System.*` first. Aliases for `ModStrings` branches come last.

1. `System.*`
2. Everything else alphabetically: `HarmonyLib`, `Isochronous`, `KMod`, `Newtonsoft.Json`, `PeterHan.PLib.*`, `ProcGenGame`, `UnityEngine`
3. Aliases (`using TOOL = SweepZones.ModStrings.UI.TOOLS.SWEEPZONES;`)

### Example
**Id:** blk-cb4940771b30

```csharp
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Reflection;
using HarmonyLib;
using Isochronous;
using Klei;
using KMod;
using STRINGS;
using UnityEngine;
```
(`mods/salty-surf/src/SaltySurf/Mod.cs`)

`Debug.Log` resolves either to `UnityEngine.Debug` or to the game's own global `Debug` class, so several `Mod.cs` files omit `using UnityEngine`. When a file imports `System.Diagnostics`, qualify the call as `UnityEngine.Debug.Log` (`mods/just-fall-already/src/JustFallAlready/FallPoke.cs`).

## Comments
**Id:** blk-da159b997542

### When to Comment
**Id:** blk-93242b225403

- On every non-trivial class, an XML `<summary>` that says what the game does and what the patch changes, so a reader can check the patch against the game code. The long summary on `OvercrowdingMonitor_UpdateRegion_Patch` in `mods/dont-count-eggs-on-rails/src/DontCountEggsOnRails/Mod.cs` is the model.
- Where a game quirk forces an odd line: `// The game's .NET Framework has no AddOrUpdate on this table.`
- Where another mod is involved, name it and its Workshop id (`mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Mod.cs`, `mods/smart-weight-plate/src/SmartWeightPlate/Mod.cs`).
- Escape angle brackets in XML comments as `<` and `>`.

### When NOT to Comment
**Id:** blk-84959e411221

- Code that reads clearly from its names.
- Commented-out code; delete it.
- Restating what a line does.

### Format
**Id:** blk-bdcb82394d6a

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// The "Any" choice. It is a tag like the elements a sensor's Filterable holds, so it rides
/// in the same saved field and copies with the building's settings.
/// </summary>
public static class AnyElement

// Single-line note for a quirk or a reason.
```

## Control Structures
**Id:** blk-278abc5927bf

### Conditionals
**Id:** blk-1de4d1f2707d

Guard clauses and early `return` or `continue` keep nesting shallow (`SettleSimBackwalls.UpdateFromSim` in `mods/natural-backwalls-everywhere/src/NaturalBackwalls/SettleSimPatch.cs`):

```csharp
if (!Grid.IsValidCell(cell))
	continue;
ushort idx = data->backwallElement[cell];
if (idx == ushort.MaxValue || idx >= elements.Count)
	continue;
```

### Loops
**Id:** blk-7bf2c80b2f8e

- Plain `for` and `foreach`. Code that runs every sim tick or frame avoids LINQ and allocations; reuse scratch lists (`scratch` in `mods/just-fall-already/src/JustFallAlready/FallPoke.cs`).
- Local types are written out (`Tech tech = ...`). `var` appears mainly in `mods/upgrade-planner`, `mods/natural-backwalls-everywhere` and the test projects; follow the surrounding file.

### Strings
**Id:** blk-a5b5ed29ed18

- Log and UI text is built with `+` concatenation, or `string.Format` on a `LocString`. String interpolation is not used in mod code.
- Player-visible text is a `LocString` field in `ModStrings`, never a literal at the call site (see [naming conventions](naming-conventions.md)).

## Harmony Patches
**Id:** blk-cfbf3f14521b

- A patch is a static class with `[HarmonyPatch(typeof(Type), nameof(Type.Method))]`, or `[HarmonyPatch(typeof(Type), "PrivateMethod")]` for a non-public method, and methods named `Prefix`, `Postfix`, `Transpiler` or `Finalizer` (`mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Patches.cs`).
- Game state arrives through Harmony parameters: `__instance`, `__result`, `___field`. Fields read repeatedly use `AccessTools.FieldRefAccess` kept in a `static readonly` field (`mods/detect-any-element/src/DetectAnyElement/Patches.cs`).
- A prefix returns `true` to let the game's method run and `false` only when it replaces the method (`mods/dont-count-eggs-on-rails`, `mods/bitshifter` `UpdateVisuals`).
- A patch that depends on an option implements `Prepare()` (`mods/jumper-bridges/src/JumperBridges/Patches.cs`); a patch with several targets implements `TargetMethods()`.
- `UserMod2.OnLoad` calls `base.OnLoad(harmony)`, which applies every patch in the assembly, then registers libraries and logs the version. A mod that must patch after all others applies its patches from `OnAllModsLoaded` instead (`mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Mod.cs`).
- Transpilers search for the instruction they change and report when it is not found; see [error handling](error-handling.md).

## Game Components
**Id:** blk-fd0855e66b70

- A component extends `KMonoBehaviour`, overrides `OnPrefabInit`, `OnSpawn` and `OnCleanUp` and calls `base` from each. Sibling components come in through `[MyCmpGet]` or `[MyCmpReq]` (`mods/no-magic-fridges/src/NoMagicFridges/FridgeThermostat.cs`).
- Saved state uses `[Serialize]` fields with `[SerializationConfig(MemberSerialization.OptIn)]` on the class (`mods/sweep-zones/src/SweepZones/ZoneStore.cs`).
- Components are added to prefabs from a `DoPostConfigureComplete` postfix with `go.AddOrGet<T>()`.

## Project-Specific Rules
**Id:** blk-8c7f61bf806a

- Mod options are a PLib `POptions` class marked `[JsonObject(MemberSerialization.OptIn)]` and `[ConfigFile(SharedConfigLocation: true)]`, read through a static `Load()` (`mods/vent-freeze-fix/src/VentFreezeFix/Options.cs`) or through `SingletonOptions<Options>` (`mods/storage-pod-redux`). Option titles are string-table keys, so the translation follows the language.
- Every mod logs one line at load: `[<Name>] Loaded version <assembly version>`.
- Tests live in a separate `<Name>.Tests` project and are written as `[OniTest]` coroutines against the real game.

### Natural Backwalls Everywhere specifics
**Id:** blk-a2d21dcff957

- The folder is `natural-backwalls-everywhere` but the project, assembly, namespace and log prefix are `NaturalBackwalls`; `staticID` is `Isochronous.NaturalBackwallsEverywhere`.
- `UsePLib`, `UseTranslations` and `ReferenceUnityUI`. The mod ships a `worldgen` folder, copied next to the DLL by the `DeployWorldgen` target in `src/NaturalBackwalls/NaturalBackwalls.csproj`.
- Patches are split by what they patch: `Patches.cs`, `PlanetoidPatch.cs`, `FeaturePatch.cs`, `SettleSimPatch.cs`, `WorldgenThreadPatch.cs`, `Census.cs`. They are `public static` classes; `Census.cs` names its patch `Game_OnSpawn_Census`.
- `SettleSimPatch.cs` uses `unsafe` code to work on the sim's update buffers.
- `Options` implements `IOptions` and builds one row per biome group at run time (`Options.cs`, `BiomeOptionsEntry.cs`, `PatternOptionsEntry.cs`); it is read again for every world generated, so changes need no restart. `using OPTIONS = ...` aliases the string branch.
- `tools/BiomePreview` is a separate WinForms project that previews biomes outside the game; it is not part of the mod DLL.

## Related
**Id:** blk-5d0eb9b42edd

- See also: [naming conventions](naming-conventions.md)
- See also: [error handling](error-handling.md)

documents.title: Error Handling Conventions
documents.text:
---
doc_id: doc-0ad8dccd6659
description: "How Natural Backwalls Everywhere guards its Harmony patches, reflection lookups and file reads, and what it logs when something is missing."
applies_to:
  - "src/**"
---
# Error Handling Conventions

## Principles
**Id:** blk-d7345384307a

1. **Never break the game for a mod's sake.** A patch that cannot do its job leaves the vanilla behaviour in place and says so in the log. It does not throw into the game's update loop.
2. **Check what you patch.** Game updates rename fields and move code. Every reflection lookup, transpiler match and prefab or tech lookup is checked for a miss.
3. **Say what degraded.** A warning names the thing that was not found and the consequence, so a bug report with `Player.log` is enough to diagnose.
4. **Don't swallow.** A `catch` logs and either returns a safe default or continues; it is never empty.
5. **Log at the right level.** `Debug.Log` for start-up and summaries, `Debug.LogWarning` for degraded behaviour, `Debug.LogError` for a failed player action.

There is no custom exception hierarchy. Mods are small patches over game code, so errors are handled where they occur.

## Guarding Patches
**Id:** blk-be03f1a912d6

### Missing member: warn, leave vanilla
**Id:** blk-4c1ca7ab8b1f

A reflection lookup that returns null is checked before use. The patch then does nothing, or returns `true` from a prefix so the game's method runs.

```csharp
if (ActiveField == null || StorageField == null)
	return true; // the game renamed its fields: leave vanilla alone rather than throw
```
(`mods/no-magic-fridges/src/NoMagicFridges/Patches.cs`; the warning is logged once at load by `SimTransferMethod` in `FridgeThermostat.cs`.)

### Transpiler: count the match
**Id:** blk-6a76d7ebba04

A transpiler counts the instructions it replaced. Zero (or more than expected) logs a warning and returns the original code, so a game update disables the change instead of breaking the method.

```csharp
if (swapped == 0)
	Debug.LogWarning("[CornerBuildAnything] " + where + " does not load OffsetGroups.InvertedStandardTable; corner reach not applied there");
```
(`mods/corner-build-anything/src/CornerBuildAnything/ReachTablePatches.cs`; same pattern in `mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Patches.cs` and `mods/natural-backwalls-everywhere/src/NaturalBackwalls/SettleSimPatch.cs`.)

### Missing data: warn, continue
**Id:** blk-ef0357ebcd1c

A build-menu, tech or asset lookup that finds nothing warns and keeps the mod working:

```csharp
Tech tech = Db.Get().Techs.TryGet(TechId);
if (tech == null)
{
	Debug.LogWarning("[SmartWeightPlate] Tech '" + TechId + "' not found; building will be unlocked from the start");
	return;
}
```
(`mods/smart-weight-plate/src/SmartWeightPlate/Patches.cs`; also `mods/multichannel-critter-sensor`, `mods/storage-pod-redux`.) Missing art or a missing vanilla prefab degrades the same way (`Display.UseAnim` in `mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Patches.cs`, `mods/multichannel-critter-sensor/src/MultichannelCritterSensor/MultichannelCritterSensorSideScreen.cs`).

### Null checks on game objects
**Id:** blk-475f58d796c4

Components and arguments that can be absent are tested before use: `if (stt == null || !Sim.IsValidHandle(stt.SimHandle)) return true;`, `if (sensor == null || GameScenePartitioner.Instance == null) return;` (`mods/motion-sensor-range/src/MotionSensorRange/RangeSlider.cs`).

### Warn once
**Id:** blk-caab886a5536

Work that repeats every frame or tick warns once behind a flag (`warnedMissingInternals` in `RangeSlider.cs`).

## try/catch
**Id:** blk-f04d3902a855

`try`/`catch (Exception e)` is used in four situations and nowhere else:

1. **Optional integration with another mod.** Patching or reading another mod's types may fail for any reason. Log the message and skip the integration (`BetterAutomationOverlayCompat.Apply` in `mods/smart-weight-plate/src/SmartWeightPlate/Mod.cs`; `mods/upgrade-planner/src/UpgradePlanner/Compat/BlueprintsCompat.cs`).
2. **File and JSON reads and writes.** Return an empty or null result (`mods/upgrade-planner/src/UpgradePlanner/Plan/Presets.cs`, `mods/storage-pod-redux/src/StoragePodRedux/ModDetection.cs`, `mods/sweep-zones/src/SweepZones/ToolIcon.cs`).
3. **Patches that run inside worldgen or per-cell work**, where an escaping exception kills a thread or a whole pass (`mods/natural-backwalls-everywhere/src/NaturalBackwalls/FeaturePatch.cs`, `PlanetoidPatch.cs`, `Patches.cs`, `Census.cs`).
4. **Per-job work in a queue**, so one failure does not stop the rest (`mods/upgrade-planner/src/UpgradePlanner/Tool/PlacementQueue.cs`, logged with `Debug.LogError`).

The message form is `"[<Name>] <what was skipped>: " + e.Message`. Use `e.GetBaseException().Message` when the exception may be a reflection wrapper, and the full `e` when the stack trace is needed.

### Finalizer for a thread with no handler
**Id:** blk-2cda0e3a8dd6

`Cluster.BeginGeneration` is the worldgen thread body and has none; an exception ends the thread and the loading screen waits forever. A finalizer reports the failure through the game's own error path and logs the exception (`Cluster_BeginGeneration_Patch` in `mods/natural-backwalls-everywhere/src/NaturalBackwalls/WorldgenThreadPatch.cs`).

## Yielding to Other Mods
**Id:** blk-016318d101d7

When another mod already does the job or shares an id, the mod steps aside and logs why:
- Bitshifter disables itself when Digital CPU is enabled or the contested methods already have Harmony owners (`WhyYield` in `mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Mod.cs`).
- Storage Pod Redux does not register its buildings while the original Storage Pod is enabled, and logs a warning telling the player to disable one (`mods/storage-pod-redux/src/StoragePodRedux/Mod.cs`).

## Logging
**Id:** blk-8bb4d3c90a73

### Log Levels
**Id:** blk-dc07f4a8abe8

| Level | Use For | Example |
|-------|---------|---------|
| `Debug.LogError` | A player action failed and was abandoned | `PlacementQueue` in `mods/upgrade-planner` |
| `Debug.LogWarning` | Degraded or skipped behaviour | the examples above |
| `Debug.Log` | Load line, a one-line summary of what a pass changed | `Tagged N refined metal(s)` in `mods/refined-building` |

### What to Include
**Id:** blk-63783d2b239e

- The `[<ModName>] ` prefix on every line; `JumperBridgesMod.LogPrefix` holds it for that mod.
- What was expected, what was found, and what the mod does instead.
- Cell numbers, building names and element ids when they identify the case (`mods/vent-freeze-fix`).
- Per-tick or per-frame telemetry only behind a debug option (`VentFreezeWatcher.Verbose`, `DebugSave.Enabled`) or capped (`DetailLines` in `SettleSimPatch.cs`).

PLib's `PUtil.Log*` helpers are not used; all mods log through `Debug`.

## Anti-Patterns to Avoid
**Id:** blk-2ab6d7b3e16c

### Swallowing exceptions
**Id:** blk-f23be92b9d7d

An empty `catch` hides a broken patch. The one `catch` that returns a fallback without a log is `GuessLanguageCode` in `common/src/Translations.cs`, because a missing language preference is the normal case before the game has started.

### Throwing from a patch
**Id:** blk-dd5003fe429c

An exception in a prefix or postfix on a per-frame or sim method repeats every frame. Guard, log once, return.

### Assuming the game's internals
**Id:** blk-4d7cded4dc3b

Reading a private field by name without a null check on the `FieldInfo`, or replacing an instruction without confirming it was found, breaks on the next game update.

### Silent degradation
**Id:** blk-ee5834add906

Doing nothing without a log line leaves a player and the author guessing. Every skipped path logs.

### Spamming the log
**Id:** blk-072cd61b19ea

A warning inside an update method fires thousands of times. Use a once-flag.

## Project-Specific Patterns
**Id:** blk-a4d21297c79b

### Natural Backwalls Everywhere specifics
**Id:** blk-7423d5bfd4b5

- Worldgen runs on a thread the game does not guard, so the patches wrap their work in `try`/`catch` and log `[NaturalBackwalls] ... skipped` with the exception message, leaving worldgen untouched (`Patches.cs`, `FeaturePatch.cs`, `PlanetoidPatch.cs`, `Census.cs`).
- `Cluster_BeginGeneration_Patch.Finalizer` turns an escaped worldgen exception into the game's failure path with a logged stack trace (`WorldgenThreadPatch.cs`).
- `WorldGenSimUtil_DoSettleSim_Patch` replaces `BackwallManager.UpdateFromSim` in the offline settle sim with `SettleSimBackwalls.UpdateFromSim`, warns when the call is not found, and logs a capped number of detail lines (`DetailLines`) plus one summary.
- Missing noise files log a warning and fall back to `FallbackNoise`.
- `ExportOverlay` and `Census` are developer features behind options; `ExportOverlay` logs `Export failed` with the exception.

## Related
**Id:** blk-35a33d4ae18c

- See also: [code style](code-style.md)
- See also: [naming conventions](naming-conventions.md)

---

description: "File, namespace, patch class, string key and id naming for Natural Backwalls Everywhere (project NaturalBackwalls)."
applies_to:

---
# Naming Conventions

## Files and Directories
**Id:** blk-529e052f8306

### General Rules
**Id:** blk-bc1605978ba1

- A mod lives in `mods/<kebab-case-name>/` (`natural-backwalls-everywhere`, `just-fall-already`).
- Its code is under `mods/<name>/src/<PascalName>/` with a matching `src/<PascalName>.Tests/` project. `AssemblyName`, `RootNamespace` and the project folder share one PascalCase name (`DontCountEggsOnRails`).
- C# files are PascalCase and named for the main type they hold. One concept per file; small related types may share a file (`Display` in `mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Patches.cs`).
- Release tags are `<mod-folder>-v<version>` (repository README).

### Examples by Type
**Id:** blk-a8ba49e2c00b

| Type | Convention | Example |
|------|------------|---------|
| Mod entry class | `Mod.cs`, class `<Name>Mod : UserMod2` | `BitshifterMod` in `Mod.cs` |
| Harmony patches | `Patches.cs`, or a file named for what is patched | `PlanetoidPatch.cs`, `SettleSimPatch.cs` |
| Building config | `<Building>Config.cs`, class `<Building>Config : IBuildingConfig` with `public const string ID` | `SmartWeightPlateConfig.cs` |
| Side screen | `<Building>SideScreen.cs` | `SmartWeightPlateSideScreen.cs` |
| Components | `<Thing>.cs` named for the component | `FridgeThermostat.cs`, `ZoneStore.cs` |
| Strings | `ModStrings.cs` | `mods/salty-surf/src/SaltySurf/ModStrings.cs` |
| Options | `Options.cs`, class `Options` | `mods/vent-freeze-fix/src/VentFreezeFix/Options.cs` |
| Tests | `<Topic>.cs` in `<Name>.Tests`, one static class per topic | `Reach.cs`, `Gates.cs`, `Persistence.cs`; `Kit.cs` for shared helpers |
| Mod metadata | `mod.yaml`, `mod_info.yaml` in the project folder | `staticID: "Isochronous.<PascalName>"` |
| Translations | `translations/<locale>.po`, template `<Name>.pot` | `mods/detect-any-element/src/DetectAnyElement/translations` |
| Art | `anim/` (kanim files), `assets/` | `bitshifter_ribbon_reader_kanim` |
| Release material | `mods/<name>/publish/`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md` | |

## Code Naming
**Id:** blk-24046c551181

### Variables
**Id:** blk-9d32bd324e3e

- camelCase for locals, parameters and private instance fields; no underscore prefix.
- PascalCase for constants (`ArmSeconds`, `Bits`, `TechId`) and for `static readonly` values that act as constants or lookups (`Standard`, `YieldToWorkshopIds`, `Contested`).
- camelCase for private static mutable state and caches (`armed`, `scratch`, `lastGrid`, `symbols`, `anyRows`).
- Descriptive names; single letters only for loop indexes and the `e` of a catch.

```csharp
private const float ArmSeconds = 2f;
private static readonly Dictionary<int, float> armed = new Dictionary<int, float>();
```
(`mods/just-fall-already/src/JustFallAlready/FallPoke.cs`)

### Functions/Methods
**Id:** blk-ea141dfef780

- PascalCase, starting with a verb: `Apply`, `Decide`, `SwapTable`, `CopyRangeFrom`, `ApplyRange`.
- Game callbacks keep the game's names (`OnSpawn`, `OnPrefabInit`, `OnCleanUp`, `Sim1000ms`).
- Harmony methods are named for their kind: `Prefix`, `Postfix`, `Transpiler`, `Finalizer`, plus `Prepare`, `TargetMethod`, `TargetMethods`.

### Classes/Types/Interfaces
**Id:** blk-dfa66a165b36

- PascalCase nouns. Interfaces take an `I` prefix (`IPlanTab` and `ITabView` in `mods/upgrade-planner`, and the game's own).
- Harmony patch classes: `<PatchedType>_<PatchedMethod>_Patch` (`LogicRibbonReader_GetBitDepth_Patch`, `Db_Initialize_Patch`, `GeneratedBuildings_LoadGeneratedBuildings_Patch`). A patch for a type with one concern may use `<Type>_Patch` (`LiquidVentConfig_Patch`). Patches nested in a holder class may drop the suffix (`Constructable_OnSpawn` in `ReachTablePatches`).
- Classes are `sealed` unless built for inheritance. The mod class is `public sealed`. Types the game does not reach are `internal`.
- Option enums and nested helper types are PascalCase (`CoolPodMode`, `BridgeKind`).

### Booleans
**Id:** blk-6937744d70bd

- Prefix with `Is`, `Has`, `Can`, `Should` or name the state: `IsEnabled`, `OriginalActive`, `isSpawned`, `warnedMissingInternals`.

### Strings (`ModStrings`)
**Id:** blk-7aecb9e1983d

- `ModStrings` mirrors the game's `STRINGS` tree: nested static classes and `LocString` fields in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE. `ModStrings.BUILDINGS.PREFABS.<BUILDINGID>.NAME` is registered as `STRINGS.BUILDINGS.PREFABS.<BUILDINGID>.NAME`, the key the game looks a building name up by (`mods/smart-weight-plate/src/SmartWeightPlate/ModStrings.cs`).
- Mod-private text goes under a branch named for the mod in capitals (`ModStrings.SALTYSURF.ELEMENT_LIST`, `ModStrings.JUMPERBRIDGES.OPTIONS`).
- Option keys are written out as `STRINGS.<MOD>.OPTIONS.<OPTION>.NAME` and `.TOOLTIP`; categories as `STRINGS.<MOD>.OPTIONS.CATEGORY.<NAME>`.
- Long branches are shortened with an alias at the top of the file (`using OPTIONS = NaturalBackwalls.ModStrings.NATURALBACKWALLS.OPTIONS;`).

### Ids and Tags
**Id:** blk-068a52f8eb11

- Building ids are PascalCase and match the config class (`SmartWeightPlate`); a mod that replaces another mod's buildings reuses that mod's ids (`StoragePodConfig`, `CoolPodConfig` in `mods/storage-pod-redux`).
- Tags and PAction ids carry a mod prefix: `DetectAnyElement_Any`, `Isochronous.SweepZones.Tool`.
- The `staticID` in `mod.yaml` is `Isochronous.<PascalName>`.
- Test names start with the mod's name or an abbreviation of it: `[OniTest("Bitshifter: a NOT gate on a ribbon inverts every bit")]`, `VFF:` for Vent Freeze Fix.

## Project-Specific Conventions
**Id:** blk-4365c851396d

### Natural Backwalls Everywhere specifics
**Id:** blk-f63e1ff3f8ed

- Biome and zone groups are UPPERCASE branches in `ModStrings.NATURALBACKWALLS` (`BIOMES`, `PATTERNS`, `ZONES`); biome group ids are the keys of the option dictionaries.
- Patch classes follow `<Type>_<Method>_Patch` (`TerrainCell_ApplyBackground_Patch`, `WorldGen_GenerateOffline_Patch`).
- Test classes: `Generated`, `Guards`, `Looks`, `Planning`, `Support` in `src/NaturalBackwalls.Tests`.

## Related
**Id:** blk-79a09c775370

- See also: [code style](code-style.md)
- See also: [error handling](error-handling.md)

---
doc_id: doc-dfa34259ff9b
description: "The things No Magic Fridges adds or patches, with file locations, gameplay rules and key code paths."
applies_to:
  - "src/NoMagicFridges/**"
---
# No Magic Fridges domain

## Overview
**Id:** blk-341e7f0208d5

No Magic Fridges changes what a powered fridge does to its contents. Vanilla attaches a simulated 1 degree C heat reservoir (400 kJ/K, 1000 W/K) to every stored item, which cools warm food but also drags deep-frozen food up to 1 degree C. The mod switches that reservoir off for fridge contents and runs its own model once a second: the fridge is an insulated box with a thermostat that only ever cools. Unpowered fridges, and items outside a fridge, are vanilla. The mod adds no building, no options and no saved state.

## Key Entities
**Id:** blk-0d6d8f812e66

### FridgeThermostat
**Id:** blk-eb78596783d5  
**Description**: The component that runs the thermal model on a fridge building. It samples every stored item each second, moves each toward one shared interior temperature, and insulates cold items from a warmer room.  
**Location**: `src/NoMagicFridges/FridgeThermostat.cs`

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| InsulationFactor | const float 0.01 | Heat-exchange scale for an insulated item, the factor an Insulated Tile uses |
| BaseHeatCapacity | const float 25 x 3.47 | The compressor's thermal mass in kDTU/K, about 25 kg of food; larger cools a full warm fridge faster |
| InsulateBand / ReleaseBand | const float 0.25 | Kelvin hysteresis before an item is insulated or released |
| MinimumStep | const float 0.0005 | Smaller temperature changes are not sent to the sim |
| MinimumTemperature | const float 1 | Never drive an item below this many kelvin |
| items | Dictionary<int, Tracked> | Per item (by instance id): whether it is insulated and its original `SurfaceArea` and `GroundTransferScale` |
| def | `RefrigeratorController.Def` | Source of the setpoint (`simulatedInternalTemperature`) and conductivity (`simulatedThermalConductivity`) |

**Relationships**: Implements `ISim1000ms`. Uses the building's `Storage` and `Operational` (`[MyCmpGet]`), each item's `PrimaryElement` and `SimTemperatureTransfer`, and subscribes to `GameHashes.OnStorageChange`. Calls the protected `SimTemperatureTransfer.SimRegister` / `SimUnregister` through cached delegates.

### Harmony patches
**Id:** blk-6075d509d0c8  
**Location**: `src/NoMagicFridges/Patches.cs`

| Patch target | Kind | Purpose |
|--------------|------|---------|
| `SimulatedTemperatureAdjuster.OnItemSimRegistered` | Prefix | For an active adjuster whose storage has a `FridgeThermostat`, sends `ModifyElementChunkTemperatureAdjuster(handle, 0, 0, 0)` and skips vanilla, so the reservoir never attaches; any other user of the adjuster runs vanilla |
| `GeneratedBuildings.LoadGeneratedBuildings` | Postfix | Adds `FridgeThermostat` to every building definition whose complete prefab has a `RefrigeratorController.Def` (Refrigerator, Mini Fridge, modded fridges) and logs the count |

The prefix reads the adjuster's private `active` and `storage` fields by reflection and falls back to vanilla if either is missing.

### Mod entry
**Id:** blk-e480792c47bc  
**Location**: `src/NoMagicFridges/Mod.cs`
`NoMagicFridgesMod` (a `UserMod2`) only logs the version. Harmony only, no PLib, no strings. Mod id `Isochronous.NoMagicFridges` (`mod.yaml`). Nothing is saved with the game; the mod can be added to or removed from an existing save.

## Business Rules
**Id:** blk-4b1cf2b79fa1

- Everything applies only while the fridge is powered (`Operational.IsActive`). When it is not, insulation is restored on every item and nothing equalises.
- Contents share heat in both directions: each item closes the fraction `1 - exp(-k*dt/C)` of its gap to the interior temperature, with `k` the def's conductivity read as W/K (1 kDTU/s/K at 1000) and `C` = mass x specific heat. Heat is conserved.
- The compressor only cools. While the contents' mean is above the setpoint (1 degree C), interior = (BaseHeatCapacity x setpoint + sum of C x T) / (BaseHeatCapacity + sum of C), which lies between the setpoint and the mean. At or below the setpoint the compressor is off and the interior is the coupling-weighted mean, so nothing pulls food up.
- A single warm item cools about as fast as in vanilla; a fridge crammed with warm food cools at roughly a fifth of the vanilla rate.
- An item colder than its room by more than 0.25 K is insulated: its `SurfaceArea` and `GroundTransferScale` are scaled by 0.01 and its sim chunk re-registered. It is released once the room is 0.25 K colder than the item. An item warmer than the room keeps exchanging with it, so a fridge in a cold room still deep-freezes food.
- Insulation is undone when the fridge loses power, the item leaves storage, or the fridge is removed.
- Power draw, the cooling and energy-saver states, storage, the full signal and spoilage rules are untouched.

## Key Code Paths
**Id:** blk-0872d6109a15

- **Per-second step**: `Sim1000ms` samples items, decides insulation, then calls `Exchange` — see `src/NoMagicFridges/FridgeThermostat.cs`
- **Heat exchange**: `Exchange(setpoint)` picks compressor-on or compressor-off interior temperature and writes `PrimaryElement.Temperature` — see `src/NoMagicFridges/FridgeThermostat.cs`
- **Insulation**: `Insulate`, `RestoreInsulation`, `Reregister` — see `src/NoMagicFridges/FridgeThermostat.cs`
- **Reservoir suppression**: the `OnItemSimRegistered` prefix — see `src/NoMagicFridges/Patches.cs`
- **Item leaves the fridge**: `OnStorageChange` restores its exchange immediately — see `src/NoMagicFridges/FridgeThermostat.cs`
- **Tests**: in-game `[OniTest]` cases in `src/NoMagicFridges.Tests/Fridges.cs` (thermostat on every fridge and nothing else, frozen food not warmed, shared temperature with heat conserved, Mini Fridge setpoint, crammed fridge rate, unpowered fridge is vanilla, insulation and release, a non-fridge keeps the vanilla reservoir)

## Related
**Id:** blk-8be45c9d80c9

- See also: [glossary](glossary.md)

# No Magic Fridges glossary

Terms for the No Magic Fridges mod. For the code behind them, see [entities](entities.md).

## Abbreviations and Acronyms
**Id:** blk-3456ea7ca0c8

| Abbreviation | Full Term | Context |
|--------------|-----------|---------|
| ONI | Oxygen Not Included | The game this mod targets |
| NMF | No Magic Fridges | Prefix of the in-game test names in `src/NoMagicFridges.Tests/` |
| DTU | Duplicant Thermal Unit | The game's heat unit; 1 kDTU = 1 kJ. Heat capacities in the code are kDTU/K |
| kDTU/s/K | kilo-DTU per second per kelvin | Conductance; the def's 1000 (W/K) reads as 1 kDTU/s/K |
| C | Heat capacity | In the model, an item's mass x specific heat; the comments also write C for degrees Celsius |

## Terms to Avoid
**Id:** blk-f014faf2eaeb

| Avoid | Use Instead | Reason |
|-------|-------------|--------|
| Magic (cooling) | Reservoir | The vanilla behaviour the mod removes is a simulated 1 degree C reservoir on every item |
| Freezer (for the building) | Refrigerator | The vanilla building is the Refrigerator; "Freezer" appears only in a code comment describing a -19 degree C cold box |
| Insulite (for the item insulation) | Insulated Tile factor | The 0.01 scale slows exchange like an Insulated Tile; Insulite stops it |

## Cross-Domain Terms
**Id:** blk-5331b50664aa

### Reservoir (simulated temperature adjuster)
**Id:** blk-f3e230c14424  
**Definition**: Vanilla's `SimulatedTemperatureAdjuster` attaches a sim heat reservoir at the fridge's `simulatedInternalTemperature` (1 degree C) to each stored item through `ModifyElementChunkTemperatureAdjuster`. It exchanges heat both ways, which is why vanilla warms frozen food.  
**Used in**: `Patches.cs`

### Thermostat
**Id:** blk-4f0bf4991185  
**Definition**: The mod's model of the fridge as an insulated box: a shared interior temperature, a compressor that only cools, and no heating.  
**Used in**: `FridgeThermostat.cs`

### Compressor on / off
**Id:** blk-cd0fd04ff662  
**Definition**: On while the mean temperature of the contents is above the setpoint; the fridge's own thermal mass (`BaseHeatCapacity`) at the setpoint is blended in and pulls the interior down. Off at or below the setpoint, when the contents only equalise among themselves.  
**Used in**: `FridgeThermostat.Exchange`

### Setpoint
**Id:** blk-23cf70bad61b  
**Definition**: The fridge's target temperature, `RefrigeratorController.Def.simulatedInternalTemperature`, 1 degree C in vanilla.  
**Used in**: `FridgeThermostat.Sim1000ms`

### Interior temperature
**Id:** blk-c63ad1f95c65  
**Definition**: The single temperature every sampled item moves toward in one step.  
**Used in**: `FridgeThermostat.Exchange`

### RefrigeratorController
**Id:** blk-5645b8195c9e  
**Definition**: The vanilla state machine (`RefrigeratorController.Def`) on the Refrigerator and Mini Fridge. Any building with this def gets a thermostat, including modded fridges.  
**Used in**: `Patches.cs`

### SimTemperatureTransfer
**Id:** blk-c77fc14f105f  
**Definition**: The component that links an item to the sim for heat exchange with the cell it sits in; `SurfaceArea` and `GroundTransferScale` set how fast.  
**Used in**: `FridgeThermostat.Insulate`

### PrimaryElement
**Id:** blk-b54dd85bb2d1  
**Definition**: The component holding an item's element, mass and temperature. Writing `Temperature` forwards to the sim chunk.  
**Used in**: `FridgeThermostat.Exchange`

### Insulated Tile factor
**Id:** blk-83c568d5faca  
**Definition**: 0.01, the thermal-conductivity scale of the Insulated Tile, applied to a cold item's exchange with a warmer room.  
**Used in**: `FridgeThermostat.InsulationFactor`

### Operational / powered
**Id:** blk-98383b78254f  
**Definition**: `Operational.IsActive` on the fridge; true while it has power. The mod's model runs only then.  
**Used in**: `FridgeThermostat.Sim1000ms`

### Sim1000ms
**Id:** blk-0efeb721f740  
**Definition**: The game's `ISim1000ms` callback, once per second of game time; the thermostat's tick.  
**Used in**: `FridgeThermostat`

## Related
**Id:** blk-3a7256bf9c1b

- See also: [entities](entities.md)

# no-magic-fridges

## What this is
**Id:** blk-9f37b243039c

No Magic Fridges is an Oxygen Not Included mod that makes a powered fridge behave like an insulated box with a thermostat. Vanilla attaches a simulated 1 degC heat reservoir to every stored item, which cools warm food but also warms deep-frozen food back up to 1 degC. With this mod a powered fridge only ever cools what is warmer than 1 degC, never heats what is colder, lets its contents share heat with each other, and insulates cold food from the room. An unpowered fridge is exactly vanilla. Version 0.2.2 is on the Steam Workshop (id 3805326379); `mod.yaml` sets `supportedContent: ALL` and `minimumSupportedBuild: 744825`.

## Where things are
**Id:** blk-5104096f454c

- `src/NoMagicFridges/`: the mod. `Mod.cs` (entry point), `Patches.cs` (stops the vanilla reservoir being attached and adds the thermostat to the fridge prefabs), `FridgeThermostat.cs` (the thermal model, run once a second), `mod.yaml`, `mod_info.yaml`.
- `src/NoMagicFridges.Tests/`: in-game tests of fridge behaviour (`Fridges.cs`).
- `publish/`: Workshop material (`workshop-description.txt`, `workshop-id.txt`).
- `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: user-facing description and release history.
- `.context/` holds `overview.md` (this file), `domains/` (entities and glossary), `standards/` (code style, error handling, naming conventions), `decisions/`, `retrospectives/`, `projects.md` and `META.md`.

documents.text:
---
doc_id: doc-46f4375d60c5
description: "C# formatting, imports, comments, Harmony patch and component conventions for No Magic Fridges (gives fridges a real thermal model), with this mod's own layout."
applies_to:
  - "src/**"
---
# Code Style Guide

## Formatting
**Id:** blk-14654fe843b2

### Indentation
**Id:** blk-345de95fe26c

- Tabs, one per level, in every `.cs` file (`mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Mod.cs`).
- Project files (`.csproj`, `common/oni-mod.props`, `common/oni-mod.targets`) use two spaces.
- Files are committed with LF line endings; Windows checkouts convert them to CRLF (`core.autocrlf` is true), so do not hand-normalise line endings.

### Line Length
**Id:** blk-d4cd6738c9b6

- No limit is configured and the repository has no `.editorconfig`.
- Wrap long calls and string concatenations after an argument or before a `+`, and indent the continuation one tab. The start-up log call in `mods/jumper-bridges/src/JumperBridges/Mod.cs` is the pattern.
- TODO(owner): decide whether to add an `.editorconfig` recording tabs and brace placement so editors enforce what the code already does.

### Braces
**Id:** blk-d9ce7c0820b3

- Opening brace on its own line (Allman) for namespaces, types, members and multi-line control blocks.
- A body of one short statement goes on the next line without braces:

```csharp
foreach (Mod mod in mods)
{
	if (!mod.IsEnabledForActiveDlc())
		continue;
	...
}
```

- Multi-line initialisers and enums end with a trailing comma (`YieldToWorkshopIds` in `mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Mod.cs`, `CoolPodMode` in `mods/storage-pod-redux/src/StoragePodRedux/Options.cs`).

## Language and Toolchain
**Id:** blk-ff07643b5942

- C# 9 on .NET Framework 4.8 (`LangVersion` 9.0 and `TargetFramework` net48 in `common/oni-mod.props`). Namespace blocks, not file-scoped namespaces; no nullable reference types.
- Mods compile against the game's own assemblies (`common/oni-mod.targets`): `Assembly-CSharp`, `Assembly-CSharp-firstpass`, `0Harmony` and Unity modules. The game's .NET Framework lacks some newer APIs (`ConditionalWeakTable.AddOrUpdate` is missing, see `mods/detect-any-element/src/DetectAnyElement/Patches.cs`).
- Optional references are switched on in the mod csproj before the targets import: `ReferenceUnityUI`, `ReferenceImageConversion`, `UsePLib` (PLib is ILRepack-merged into the mod DLL) and `UseTranslations` (compiles `common/src/Translations.cs` in).
- One namespace per mod, equal to its `RootNamespace`. Subfolders organise files and do not add namespaces (`mods/upgrade-planner/src/UpgradePlanner/Plan`, `Rules`, `Tool`, `UI` all declare `namespace UpgradePlanner`).

## Imports/Includes
**Id:** blk-cf37994c4c5b

### Organization
**Id:** blk-e6d1725a2493

`using` directives sit above the namespace, in one block with no blank lines, sorted alphabetically with `System.*` first. Aliases for `ModStrings` branches come last.

1. `System.*`
2. Everything else alphabetically: `HarmonyLib`, `Isochronous`, `KMod`, `Newtonsoft.Json`, `PeterHan.PLib.*`, `ProcGenGame`, `UnityEngine`
3. Aliases (`using TOOL = SweepZones.ModStrings.UI.TOOLS.SWEEPZONES;`)

### Example
**Id:** blk-cd84394283fa

```csharp
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Reflection;
using HarmonyLib;
using Isochronous;
using Klei;
using KMod;
using STRINGS;
using UnityEngine;
```
(`mods/salty-surf/src/SaltySurf/Mod.cs`)

`Debug.Log` resolves either to `UnityEngine.Debug` or to the game's own global `Debug` class, so several `Mod.cs` files omit `using UnityEngine`. When a file imports `System.Diagnostics`, qualify the call as `UnityEngine.Debug.Log` (`mods/just-fall-already/src/JustFallAlready/FallPoke.cs`).

## Comments
**Id:** blk-daafd1797aa8

### When to Comment
**Id:** blk-f989724353cb

- On every non-trivial class, an XML `<summary>` that says what the game does and what the patch changes, so a reader can check the patch against the game code. The long summary on `OvercrowdingMonitor_UpdateRegion_Patch` in `mods/dont-count-eggs-on-rails/src/DontCountEggsOnRails/Mod.cs` is the model.
- Where a game quirk forces an odd line: `// The game's .NET Framework has no AddOrUpdate on this table.`
- Where another mod is involved, name it and its Workshop id (`mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Mod.cs`, `mods/smart-weight-plate/src/SmartWeightPlate/Mod.cs`).
- Escape angle brackets in XML comments as `<` and `>`.

### When NOT to Comment
**Id:** blk-8704337db0af

- Code that reads clearly from its names.
- Commented-out code; delete it.
- Restating what a line does.

### Format
**Id:** blk-bfd8c830f9b5

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// The "Any" choice. It is a tag like the elements a sensor's Filterable holds, so it rides
/// in the same saved field and copies with the building's settings.
/// </summary>
public static class AnyElement

// Single-line note for a quirk or a reason.
```

## Control Structures
**Id:** blk-951963141f64

### Conditionals
**Id:** blk-3f366bdebdc6

Guard clauses and early `return` or `continue` keep nesting shallow (`SettleSimBackwalls.UpdateFromSim` in `mods/natural-backwalls-everywhere/src/NaturalBackwalls/SettleSimPatch.cs`):

```csharp
if (!Grid.IsValidCell(cell))
	continue;
ushort idx = data->backwallElement[cell];
if (idx == ushort.MaxValue || idx >= elements.Count)
	continue;
```

### Loops
**Id:** blk-7e5838a4ab04

- Plain `for` and `foreach`. Code that runs every sim tick or frame avoids LINQ and allocations; reuse scratch lists (`scratch` in `mods/just-fall-already/src/JustFallAlready/FallPoke.cs`).
- Local types are written out (`Tech tech = ...`). `var` appears mainly in `mods/upgrade-planner`, `mods/natural-backwalls-everywhere` and the test projects; follow the surrounding file.

### Strings
**Id:** blk-0ad7bc6dca06

- Log and UI text is built with `+` concatenation, or `string.Format` on a `LocString`. String interpolation is not used in mod code.
- Player-visible text is a `LocString` field in `ModStrings`, never a literal at the call site (see [naming conventions](naming-conventions.md)).

## Harmony Patches
**Id:** blk-d44c4a153c1c

- A patch is a static class with `[HarmonyPatch(typeof(Type), nameof(Type.Method))]`, or `[HarmonyPatch(typeof(Type), "PrivateMethod")]` for a non-public method, and methods named `Prefix`, `Postfix`, `Transpiler` or `Finalizer` (`mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Patches.cs`).
- Game state arrives through Harmony parameters: `__instance`, `__result`, `___field`. Fields read repeatedly use `AccessTools.FieldRefAccess` kept in a `static readonly` field (`mods/detect-any-element/src/DetectAnyElement/Patches.cs`).
- A prefix returns `true` to let the game's method run and `false` only when it replaces the method (`mods/dont-count-eggs-on-rails`, `mods/bitshifter` `UpdateVisuals`).
- A patch that depends on an option implements `Prepare()` (`mods/jumper-bridges/src/JumperBridges/Patches.cs`); a patch with several targets implements `TargetMethods()`.
- `UserMod2.OnLoad` calls `base.OnLoad(harmony)`, which applies every patch in the assembly, then registers libraries and logs the version. A mod that must patch after all others applies its patches from `OnAllModsLoaded` instead (`mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Mod.cs`).
- Transpilers search for the instruction they change and report when it is not found; see [error handling](error-handling.md).

## Game Components
**Id:** blk-d12bc1aff49d

- A component extends `KMonoBehaviour`, overrides `OnPrefabInit`, `OnSpawn` and `OnCleanUp` and calls `base` from each. Sibling components come in through `[MyCmpGet]` or `[MyCmpReq]` (`mods/no-magic-fridges/src/NoMagicFridges/FridgeThermostat.cs`).
- Saved state uses `[Serialize]` fields with `[SerializationConfig(MemberSerialization.OptIn)]` on the class (`mods/sweep-zones/src/SweepZones/ZoneStore.cs`).
- Components are added to prefabs from a `DoPostConfigureComplete` postfix with `go.AddOrGet<T>()`.

## Project-Specific Rules
**Id:** blk-447262e58ac0

- Mod options are a PLib `POptions` class marked `[JsonObject(MemberSerialization.OptIn)]` and `[ConfigFile(SharedConfigLocation: true)]`, read through a static `Load()` (`mods/vent-freeze-fix/src/VentFreezeFix/Options.cs`) or through `SingletonOptions<Options>` (`mods/storage-pod-redux`). Option titles are string-table keys, so the translation follows the language.
- Every mod logs one line at load: `[<Name>] Loaded version <assembly version>`.
- Tests live in a separate `<Name>.Tests` project and are written as `[OniTest]` coroutines against the real game.

### No Magic Fridges specifics
**Id:** blk-6a0e4de0eca7

- `Patches.cs` is a `public static class Patches` with nested patch classes. `FridgeThermostat` is a `KMonoBehaviour` with `[MyCmpGet]` fields and a static `EventSystem.IntraObjectHandler` named `OnStorageChangeDelegate` (`src/NoMagicFridges/FridgeThermostat.cs`).
- Private game members are reached through `static readonly FieldInfo` fields (`ActiveField`, `StorageField`) and delegates built with `AccessTools.MethodDelegate`.
- `Mod.cs` has no `using UnityEngine`; `Debug` is the game's global class.
- No PLib, no translations, no options.

## Related
**Id:** blk-bd3ceaae837b

- See also: [naming conventions](naming-conventions.md)
- See also: [error handling](error-handling.md)

documents.text:
---
doc_id: doc-aea927ed3ec9
description: "How No Magic Fridges guards its Harmony patches, reflection lookups and file reads, and what it logs when something is missing."
applies_to:
  - "src/**"
---
# Error Handling Conventions

## Principles
**Id:** blk-dca3e40e96f1

1. **Never break the game for a mod's sake.** A patch that cannot do its job leaves the vanilla behaviour in place and says so in the log. It does not throw into the game's update loop.
2. **Check what you patch.** Game updates rename fields and move code. Every reflection lookup, transpiler match and prefab or tech lookup is checked for a miss.
3. **Say what degraded.** A warning names the thing that was not found and the consequence, so a bug report with `Player.log` is enough to diagnose.
4. **Don't swallow.** A `catch` logs and either returns a safe default or continues; it is never empty.
5. **Log at the right level.** `Debug.Log` for start-up and summaries, `Debug.LogWarning` for degraded behaviour, `Debug.LogError` for a failed player action.

There is no custom exception hierarchy. Mods are small patches over game code, so errors are handled where they occur.

## Guarding Patches
**Id:** blk-6c1ccfcd2872

### Missing member: warn, leave vanilla
**Id:** blk-b63008570ba1

A reflection lookup that returns null is checked before use. The patch then does nothing, or returns `true` from a prefix so the game's method runs.

```csharp
if (ActiveField == null || StorageField == null)
	return true; // the game renamed its fields: leave vanilla alone rather than throw
```
(`mods/no-magic-fridges/src/NoMagicFridges/Patches.cs`; the warning is logged once at load by `SimTransferMethod` in `FridgeThermostat.cs`.)

### Transpiler: count the match
**Id:** blk-1987e6421398

A transpiler counts the instructions it replaced. Zero (or more than expected) logs a warning and returns the original code, so a game update disables the change instead of breaking the method.

```csharp
if (swapped == 0)
	Debug.LogWarning("[CornerBuildAnything] " + where + " does not load OffsetGroups.InvertedStandardTable; corner reach not applied there");
```
(`mods/corner-build-anything/src/CornerBuildAnything/ReachTablePatches.cs`; same pattern in `mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Patches.cs` and `mods/natural-backwalls-everywhere/src/NaturalBackwalls/SettleSimPatch.cs`.)

### Missing data: warn, continue
**Id:** blk-2862c2be79f7

A build-menu, tech or asset lookup that finds nothing warns and keeps the mod working:

```csharp
Tech tech = Db.Get().Techs.TryGet(TechId);
if (tech == null)
{
	Debug.LogWarning("[SmartWeightPlate] Tech '" + TechId + "' not found; building will be unlocked from the start");
	return;
}
```
(`mods/smart-weight-plate/src/SmartWeightPlate/Patches.cs`; also `mods/multichannel-critter-sensor`, `mods/storage-pod-redux`.) Missing art or a missing vanilla prefab degrades the same way (`Display.UseAnim` in `mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Patches.cs`, `mods/multichannel-critter-sensor/src/MultichannelCritterSensor/MultichannelCritterSensorSideScreen.cs`).

### Null checks on game objects
**Id:** blk-d6d515fe70fe

Components and arguments that can be absent are tested before use: `if (stt == null || !Sim.IsValidHandle(stt.SimHandle)) return true;`, `if (sensor == null || GameScenePartitioner.Instance == null) return;` (`mods/motion-sensor-range/src/MotionSensorRange/RangeSlider.cs`).

### Warn once
**Id:** blk-2f4fb43549c4

Work that repeats every frame or tick warns once behind a flag (`warnedMissingInternals` in `RangeSlider.cs`).

## try/catch
**Id:** blk-0ed545257e4e

`try`/`catch (Exception e)` is used in four situations and nowhere else:

1. **Optional integration with another mod.** Patching or reading another mod's types may fail for any reason. Log the message and skip the integration (`BetterAutomationOverlayCompat.Apply` in `mods/smart-weight-plate/src/SmartWeightPlate/Mod.cs`; `mods/upgrade-planner/src/UpgradePlanner/Compat/BlueprintsCompat.cs`).
2. **File and JSON reads and writes.** Return an empty or null result (`mods/upgrade-planner/src/UpgradePlanner/Plan/Presets.cs`, `mods/storage-pod-redux/src/StoragePodRedux/ModDetection.cs`, `mods/sweep-zones/src/SweepZones/ToolIcon.cs`).
3. **Patches that run inside worldgen or per-cell work**, where an escaping exception kills a thread or a whole pass (`mods/natural-backwalls-everywhere/src/NaturalBackwalls/FeaturePatch.cs`, `PlanetoidPatch.cs`, `Patches.cs`, `Census.cs`).
4. **Per-job work in a queue**, so one failure does not stop the rest (`mods/upgrade-planner/src/UpgradePlanner/Tool/PlacementQueue.cs`, logged with `Debug.LogError`).

The message form is `"[<Name>] <what was skipped>: " + e.Message`. Use `e.GetBaseException().Message` when the exception may be a reflection wrapper, and the full `e` when the stack trace is needed.

### Finalizer for a thread with no handler
**Id:** blk-561d6f59d166

`Cluster.BeginGeneration` is the worldgen thread body and has none; an exception ends the thread and the loading screen waits forever. A finalizer reports the failure through the game's own error path and logs the exception (`Cluster_BeginGeneration_Patch` in `mods/natural-backwalls-everywhere/src/NaturalBackwalls/WorldgenThreadPatch.cs`).

## Yielding to Other Mods
**Id:** blk-0eb8c73385d0

When another mod already does the job or shares an id, the mod steps aside and logs why:
- Bitshifter disables itself when Digital CPU is enabled or the contested methods already have Harmony owners (`WhyYield` in `mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Mod.cs`).
- Storage Pod Redux does not register its buildings while the original Storage Pod is enabled, and logs a warning telling the player to disable one (`mods/storage-pod-redux/src/StoragePodRedux/Mod.cs`).

## Logging
**Id:** blk-61495414a8c6

### Log Levels
**Id:** blk-cfaac579624e

| Level | Use For | Example |
|-------|---------|---------|
| `Debug.LogError` | A player action failed and was abandoned | `PlacementQueue` in `mods/upgrade-planner` |
| `Debug.LogWarning` | Degraded or skipped behaviour | the examples above |
| `Debug.Log` | Load line, a one-line summary of what a pass changed | `Tagged N refined metal(s)` in `mods/refined-building` |

### What to Include
**Id:** blk-740fc524f68b

- The `[<ModName>] ` prefix on every line; `JumperBridgesMod.LogPrefix` holds it for that mod.
- What was expected, what was found, and what the mod does instead.
- Cell numbers, building names and element ids when they identify the case (`mods/vent-freeze-fix`).
- Per-tick or per-frame telemetry only behind a debug option (`VentFreezeWatcher.Verbose`, `DebugSave.Enabled`) or capped (`DetailLines` in `SettleSimPatch.cs`).

PLib's `PUtil.Log*` helpers are not used; all mods log through `Debug`.

## Anti-Patterns to Avoid
**Id:** blk-019dfcac4e1f

### Swallowing exceptions
**Id:** blk-0721293f3a50

An empty `catch` hides a broken patch. The one `catch` that returns a fallback without a log is `GuessLanguageCode` in `common/src/Translations.cs`, because a missing language preference is the normal case before the game has started.

### Throwing from a patch
**Id:** blk-6ca5951ac246

An exception in a prefix or postfix on a per-frame or sim method repeats every frame. Guard, log once, return.

### Assuming the game's internals
**Id:** blk-37cbf49b0752

Reading a private field by name without a null check on the `FieldInfo`, or replacing an instruction without confirming it was found, breaks on the next game update.

### Silent degradation
**Id:** blk-18072cab8ffd

Doing nothing without a log line leaves a player and the author guessing. Every skipped path logs.

### Spamming the log
**Id:** blk-ef06216f4f4e

A warning inside an update method fires thousands of times. Use a once-flag.

## Project-Specific Patterns
**Id:** blk-02aae3cd2120

### No Magic Fridges specifics
**Id:** blk-79ad1c265438

- `SimulatedTemperatureAdjuster_OnItemSimRegistered_Patch.Prefix` returns `true` (vanilla) for a null `stt`, an invalid sim handle, missing fields, an inactive adjuster and any storage without a `FridgeThermostat`. It returns `false` only for fridge storage.
- `SimTransferMethod` warns once at load when a protected `SimTemperatureTransfer` method is gone and returns null; the thermostat then does nothing and fridge contents keep vanilla behaviour.
- `GeneratedBuildings_LoadGeneratedBuildings_Patch` logs one summary line with the number of fridges that got a thermostat.

## Related
**Id:** blk-c508df09c2a7

- See also: [code style](code-style.md)
- See also: [naming conventions](naming-conventions.md)

documents.title: Naming Conventions
documents.text:
---
doc_id: doc-9f3021f06f42
description: "File, namespace, patch class, string key and id naming for No Magic Fridges (project NoMagicFridges)."
applies_to:
  - "src/**"
---
# Naming Conventions

## Files and Directories
**Id:** blk-bba4fc9ca547

### General Rules
**Id:** blk-6b6aa58612cf

- A mod lives in `mods/<kebab-case-name>/` (`natural-backwalls-everywhere`, `just-fall-already`).
- Its code is under `mods/<name>/src/<PascalName>/` with a matching `src/<PascalName>.Tests/` project. `AssemblyName`, `RootNamespace` and the project folder share one PascalCase name (`DontCountEggsOnRails`).
- C# files are PascalCase and named for the main type they hold. One concept per file; small related types may share a file (`Display` in `mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Patches.cs`).
- Release tags are `<mod-folder>-v<version>` (repository README).

### Examples by Type
**Id:** blk-c63d3276e032

| Type | Convention | Example |
|------|------------|---------|
| Mod entry class | `Mod.cs`, class `<Name>Mod : UserMod2` | `BitshifterMod` in `Mod.cs` |
| Harmony patches | `Patches.cs`, or a file named for what is patched | `PlanetoidPatch.cs`, `SettleSimPatch.cs` |
| Building config | `<Building>Config.cs`, class `<Building>Config : IBuildingConfig` with `public const string ID` | `SmartWeightPlateConfig.cs` |
| Side screen | `<Building>SideScreen.cs` | `SmartWeightPlateSideScreen.cs` |
| Components | `<Thing>.cs` named for the component | `FridgeThermostat.cs`, `ZoneStore.cs` |
| Strings | `ModStrings.cs` | `mods/salty-surf/src/SaltySurf/ModStrings.cs` |
| Options | `Options.cs`, class `Options` | `mods/vent-freeze-fix/src/VentFreezeFix/Options.cs` |
| Tests | `<Topic>.cs` in `<Name>.Tests`, one static class per topic | `Reach.cs`, `Gates.cs`, `Persistence.cs`; `Kit.cs` for shared helpers |
| Mod metadata | `mod.yaml`, `mod_info.yaml` in the project folder | `staticID: "Isochronous.<PascalName>"` |
| Translations | `translations/<locale>.po`, template `<Name>.pot` | `mods/detect-any-element/src/DetectAnyElement/translations` |
| Art | `anim/` (kanim files), `assets/` | `bitshifter_ribbon_reader_kanim` |
| Release material | `mods/<name>/publish/`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md` | |

## Code Naming
**Id:** blk-f3645b24b3c6

### Variables
**Id:** blk-a215876c0bad

- camelCase for locals, parameters and private instance fields; no underscore prefix.
- PascalCase for constants (`ArmSeconds`, `Bits`, `TechId`) and for `static readonly` values that act as constants or lookups (`Standard`, `YieldToWorkshopIds`, `Contested`).
- camelCase for private static mutable state and caches (`armed`, `scratch`, `lastGrid`, `symbols`, `anyRows`).
- Descriptive names; single letters only for loop indexes and the `e` of a catch.

```csharp
private const float ArmSeconds = 2f;
private static readonly Dictionary<int, float> armed = new Dictionary<int, float>();
```
(`mods/just-fall-already/src/JustFallAlready/FallPoke.cs`)

### Functions/Methods
**Id:** blk-808a26502d80

- PascalCase, starting with a verb: `Apply`, `Decide`, `SwapTable`, `CopyRangeFrom`, `ApplyRange`.
- Game callbacks keep the game's names (`OnSpawn`, `OnPrefabInit`, `OnCleanUp`, `Sim1000ms`).
- Harmony methods are named for their kind: `Prefix`, `Postfix`, `Transpiler`, `Finalizer`, plus `Prepare`, `TargetMethod`, `TargetMethods`.

### Classes/Types/Interfaces
**Id:** blk-02d498e998ad

- PascalCase nouns. Interfaces take an `I` prefix (`IPlanTab` and `ITabView` in `mods/upgrade-planner`, and the game's own).
- Harmony patch classes: `<PatchedType>_<PatchedMethod>_Patch` (`LogicRibbonReader_GetBitDepth_Patch`, `Db_Initialize_Patch`, `GeneratedBuildings_LoadGeneratedBuildings_Patch`). A patch for a type with one concern may use `<Type>_Patch` (`LiquidVentConfig_Patch`). Patches nested in a holder class may drop the suffix (`Constructable_OnSpawn` in `ReachTablePatches`).
- Classes are `sealed` unless built for inheritance. The mod class is `public sealed`. Types the game does not reach are `internal`.
- Option enums and nested helper types are PascalCase (`CoolPodMode`, `BridgeKind`).

### Booleans
**Id:** blk-442cb8ba03eb

- Prefix with `Is`, `Has`, `Can`, `Should` or name the state: `IsEnabled`, `OriginalActive`, `isSpawned`, `warnedMissingInternals`.

### Strings (`ModStrings`)
**Id:** blk-d957b27e2faf

- `ModStrings` mirrors the game's `STRINGS` tree: nested static classes and `LocString` fields in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE. `ModStrings.BUILDINGS.PREFABS.<BUILDINGID>.NAME` is registered as `STRINGS.BUILDINGS.PREFABS.<BUILDINGID>.NAME`, the key the game looks a building name up by (`mods/smart-weight-plate/src/SmartWeightPlate/ModStrings.cs`).
- Mod-private text goes under a branch named for the mod in capitals (`ModStrings.SALTYSURF.ELEMENT_LIST`, `ModStrings.JUMPERBRIDGES.OPTIONS`).
- Option keys are written out as `STRINGS.<MOD>.OPTIONS.<OPTION>.NAME` and `.TOOLTIP`; categories as `STRINGS.<MOD>.OPTIONS.CATEGORY.<NAME>`.
- Long branches are shortened with an alias at the top of the file (`using OPTIONS = NaturalBackwalls.ModStrings.NATURALBACKWALLS.OPTIONS;`).

### Ids and Tags
**Id:** blk-5cd11d93519d

- Building ids are PascalCase and match the config class (`SmartWeightPlate`); a mod that replaces another mod's buildings reuses that mod's ids (`StoragePodConfig`, `CoolPodConfig` in `mods/storage-pod-redux`).
- Tags and PAction ids carry a mod prefix: `DetectAnyElement_Any`, `Isochronous.SweepZones.Tool`.
- The `staticID` in `mod.yaml` is `Isochronous.<PascalName>`.
- Test names start with the mod's name or an abbreviation of it: `[OniTest("Bitshifter: a NOT gate on a ribbon inverts every bit")]`, `VFF:` for Vent Freeze Fix.

## Project-Specific Conventions
**Id:** blk-68b632fb9946

### No Magic Fridges specifics
**Id:** blk-f148924a5693

- Patch classes are nested in `Patches`: `SimulatedTemperatureAdjuster_OnItemSimRegistered_Patch`, `GeneratedBuildings_LoadGeneratedBuildings_Patch`.
- Component fields are camelCase (`storage`, `operational`, `items`); the nested helper types `Tracked` (class) and `Sample` (struct) are private.
- Test class `Fridges` in `src/NoMagicFridges.Tests/Fridges.cs`.
- Log prefix `[NoMagicFridges]`; `staticID` `Isochronous.NoMagicFridges`.

## Related
**Id:** blk-b70664fed2a4

- See also: [code style](code-style.md)
- See also: [error handling](error-handling.md)

# Refined Building domain

## Overview
**Id:** blk-0fa48a39c914

Refined Building lets every refined metal stand in wherever a building recipe asks for raw Metal Ore. It does this by adding the `Metal` tag to every solid element that carries `RefinedMetal` but not `Metal`, once, right after the game loads its element table. It adds no building, no component, no options and no saved state, so it can be added to or removed from an existing save. The mod is retired on the Workshop: another mod there already does the same job (`publish/retired.txt`).

## Key Entities
**Id:** blk-4255333b0ff3

### ElementLoader_Load_Patch
**Id:** blk-e1d4c3dc435f  
**Description**: The mod's only code of substance: a Harmony postfix on `ElementLoader.Load`. It walks `ElementLoader.elements`, skips non-solids, skips elements that lack `GameTags.RefinedMetal` or already have `GameTags.Metal`, and appends `GameTags.Metal` to the element's `oreTags`. It logs `Tagged N refined metal(s) as raw metal: ...`.  
**Location**: `src/RefinedBuilding/Patches.cs`

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| element.oreTags | Tag[] | The tag array the patch extends with `Metal` |

**Relationships**: `ElementLoader` only creates elements whose DLC is enabled and folds `materialCategory: RefinedMetal` into `oreTags`, so the loaded table covers the base game, enabled DLCs and elements other mods define. The material selector in the build menu matches recipes on tags, so the tagged metals appear beside the ores in the lists of `MATERIALS.RAW_METALS`, `MATERIALS.ALL_METALS` and the `BuildableRaw&Metal` group.

### Mod entry
**Id:** blk-e6f82a0713e3  
**Location**: `src/RefinedBuilding/Mod.cs`
`RefinedBuildingMod` (a `UserMod2`) only logs the version. No PLib, no strings, no translations. Mod id `Isochronous.RefinedBuilding` (`mod.yaml`).

## Business Rules
**Id:** blk-68956ddc3d8d

- Every loaded solid element tagged `RefinedMetal` ends up with the `Metal` tag, exactly once.
- Elements that already carry both tags in vanilla (Steel, Niobium, Thermium, Iridium) are left alone. On the current game with all DLCs the mod adds the tag to Copper, Iron, Gold, Lead, Aluminum, Tungsten, Cobalt, Nickel, Zinc, Solid Mercury and Depleted Uranium.
- Minerals, fuels, liquids, gases and raw ores are never retagged; raw ores keep `Metal`.
- Buildings that ask for Refined Metal or for raw minerals only (regular pipes, ladders, plain tiles) are unchanged.
- Discovery is unchanged: a metal appears in the build menu once it is discovered and available, like an ore.
- Refined metal debris now satisfies deliveries that ask for any Metal, such as the Oxygen Mask Station; storage filters key on the material category, so refined metals stay under Refined Metal there.
- The Metal Refinery and Rock Crusher build recipes from the same tag but skip anything without an ore-to-metal transition, so no new recipes appear.

## Key Code Paths
**Id:** blk-f6b9d46b071d

- **Retagging at load**: the `ElementLoader.Load` postfix — see `src/RefinedBuilding/Patches.cs`
- **Tests**: in-game `[OniTest]` cases in `src/RefinedBuilding.Tests/RefinedMetals.cs` (every solid refined metal has `Metal` once; minerals, fuels, liquids and gases do not gain it; a loose refined pile counts as Metal for deliveries; wire and gas pipe offer refined metals; mineral-only and Refined Metal buildings untouched; the refinery and crusher gain no self-recipe)

## Related
**Id:** blk-8ef648f9082a

- See also: [glossary](glossary.md)

# Refined Building glossary

Terms for the Refined Building mod. For the code behind them, see [entities](entities.md).

## Abbreviations and Acronyms
**Id:** blk-2daabcea9b32

| Abbreviation | Full Term | Context |
|--------------|-----------|---------|
| ONI | Oxygen Not Included | The game this mod targets |
| DLC | Downloadable content | Spaced Out, Frosty Planet and others; `ElementLoader` loads only elements of enabled DLCs |

## Terms to Avoid
**Id:** blk-199a729f1e95

| Avoid | Use Instead | Reason |
|-------|-------------|--------|
| Raw metal (for any metal) | Metal Ore / the `Metal` tag | "Raw" means unrefined ore; the mod makes refined metals count as that tag, they do not become ore |
| Pipes, ladders, plain tiles as affected buildings | Wire, pneumatic doors, mesh tiles, batteries, pumps, valves, vents | The early description named buildings that are built from raw minerals and never took metal (fixed in 1.0.1) |

## Cross-Domain Terms
**Id:** blk-594839f51b52

### Metal (tag)
**Id:** blk-d237716673b4  
**Definition**: `GameTags.Metal`. The tag building recipes match when they ask for "Metal Ore". Raw metal ores carry it; the mod adds it to refined metals.  
**Used in**: `Patches.cs`

### RefinedMetal (tag)
**Id:** blk-830e38f6d68e  
**Definition**: `GameTags.RefinedMetal`. The tag of refined metal elements (from `materialCategory: RefinedMetal`); the mod's filter.  
**Used in**: `Patches.cs`

### oreTags
**Id:** blk-501ed9940ebc  
**Definition**: The tag array on an `Element` that `ElementLoader` fills from its material category. The mod appends `Metal` to it.  
**Used in**: `Patches.cs`

### MATERIALS.RAW_METALS / ALL_METALS
**Id:** blk-d2a4e6688b06  
**Definition**: The game's material-category lists a building recipe names. Despite its name `ALL_METALS` is also just `{"Metal"}`; the `BuildableRaw&Metal` group (gas pipes, storage bins, wash basins) also matches the tag.  
**Used in**: `README.md`

### ElementLoader
**Id:** blk-17f70d2804d2  
**Definition**: The game class that loads the element table; `ElementLoader.Load` is patched and `ElementLoader.elements` is the loaded list.  
**Used in**: `Patches.cs`

### Refined Metal (material)
**Id:** blk-5e045b8ba0c0  
**Definition**: The material category buildings such as the Metal Refinery's outputs belong to (Copper, Iron, Steel and so on). Buildings that ask for Refined Metal are untouched.  
**Used in**: `README.md`

### Metal Refinery and Rock Crusher
**Id:** blk-45c15c79ef6f  
**Definition**: Buildings that build recipe lists from the same tag. They skip anything without an ore-to-metal transition, so the mod adds no recipe to them.  
**Used in**: `RefinedMetals.cs` tests

## Related
**Id:** blk-fdc9cbe0e3b5

- See also: [entities](entities.md)

# refined-building

## What this is
**Id:** blk-d87d99e6bbcc

Refined Building is an Oxygen Not Included mod that lets every refined metal be used wherever a building asks for raw Metal Ore: wire, pneumatic doors and airlocks, mesh tiles, batteries, pumps, valves, vents, coal generators, the electrolyzer, sinks and showers. After the game loads its element table, every solid element tagged `RefinedMetal` that lacks the `Metal` tag gets it, so the refined metals appear in those buildings' material lists. It finds the metals at runtime, so it covers the base game, the enabled DLCs and refined metals added by other mods. Buildings that ask for Refined Metal are untouched. It does the same job as Cairath's Refined Metals Usable As Raw Metals, without a fixed list. Version 1.0.1 is built; `publish/retired.txt` records that the mod is unlisted on the Workshop (id 3806989781) because an existing mod already does this job. `mod.yaml` sets `supportedContent: ALL` and `minimumSupportedBuild: 744825`.

## Where things are
**Id:** blk-eecf05761bd9

- `src/RefinedBuilding/`: the mod. `Mod.cs` (entry point), `Patches.cs` (the postfix on `ElementLoader.Load` that tags the metals), `mod.yaml`, `mod_info.yaml`.
- `src/RefinedBuilding.Tests/`: in-game tests (`RefinedMetals.cs`).
- `publish/`: Workshop material (`workshop-description.txt`, `workshop-id.txt`, `retired.txt`).
- `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: user-facing description and release history.
- `.context/` holds `overview.md` (this file), `domains/` (entities and glossary), `standards/` (code style, error handling, naming conventions), `decisions/`, `retrospectives/`, `projects.md` and `META.md`.
